press: e.g. the Examiner 496 (29 June 1817) 406; 498 (13 July 1817) 435. This allusion to the horrors of
slavery, combined with the British government’s role in the indefinite postponement of the abolition
of the international trade in slaves in 1815, makes the similes in this stanza grimly apt to the Foreign
